observations: Photo 0: Back of a light purple iPhone with a single camera lens and Apple logo. The phone appears to be an iPhone 13 or 14 series due to the camera module design and shape. No visible damage to the back glass.

Photo 1: Screen shows 'Battery Health' with Maximum Capacity at 92%, Cycle Count at 337, Manufacture Date August 2025, and First Use January 2026. The date is impossible — August 2025 is in the future, and First Use in January 2026 is even further ahead. This suggests the photo is fake or manipulated.
Photo 2: Side view of the phone showing volume buttons and power button. The side appears intact, but no visible damage is shown. The screen is on, indicating the phone is powered.

read_from: photo 0 back panel with Apple logo and camera design

claims.evidence: The term 'iPhone Air' is not a real model. The photos show an iPhone with a single rear camera, likely an iPhone 13 or 14 series, but no model name is visible. The '256gb' claim cannot be verified from the photos.
The screen is on and shows battery health, but this does not prove all functions (camera, speakers, charging, etc.) are working. No video or additional photos show functionality.

risks.risk: Fake or manipulated photos — the battery health screen shows a future manufacture date (August 2025) and first use (January 2026), which is impossible.
risks.proof: A real screenshot of the battery health with correct dates, or a video showing the phone in use with real-time date and time.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially fake or non-functional, with severe discount for lack of trust.

risks.risk: Incorrect model — 'iPhone Air' is not a real model; the phone may be an older or lower-end model than claimed.
risks.proof: Photo of the front screen showing the model name in Settings > General > About Phone, or a clear shot of the model number on the back or in the box.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as an unknown iPhone model, likely lower-end, with discount for uncertainty.

risks.risk: Storage capacity not verified — the seller claims 256GB, but no photo shows the storage info.
risks.proof: Photo of Settings > General > iPhone Storage showing 256GB total capacity.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unknown storage, likely lower than 256GB, with discount.

risks.risk: Physical damage not visible — the photos show only one side and a partial side view; screen, front glass, and internal components are not shown.
risks.proof: Full 360-degree photos or video showing all sides, screen, and ports.
risks.if_unproven: Priced with assumption of minor to moderate wear, with discount for hidden damage.

proof_requests: Photo of Settings > General > About Phone showing the exact model name and storage capacity.
Video or photo showing the phone's front screen with real-time date and time (to verify the battery health screen is not fake).
Full 360-degree photos of the phone, including screen, front, back, and all edges.
Photo of the original box or receipt if available.
response.reason: The battery health screen shows impossible future dates, indicating the photo may be fake. The model 'iPhone Air' does not exist, and the storage capacity is unverified. Without proof of authenticity and real-time functionality, the item cannot be priced reliably.
